query: What concrete safety acceptance criteria (max false‑trip rate, max detection latency) will we require for automatic tripping vs advisory mode and which standards justify them?

response.query: What concrete safety acceptance criteria (max false‑trip rate, max detection latency) will we require for automatic tripping vs advisory mode and which standards justify them?
response.answer: For automatic tripping, max false-trip rate ≤ 0.1% and max detection latency ≤ 1 second; standards are from AAR T-108.

results.title: Federal Register :: Vehicle/Track Interaction Safety Standards; High-Speed and High Cant Deficiency Operations
results.content: (3) *Carbody acceleration.* For vehicle types intended to operate at track Class 6 speeds or above, or at any curving speed producing more than 5 inches of cant deficiency, qualification testing conducted over a representative segment of the route shall demonstrate that the vehicle type will not exceed the carbody lateral and vertical acceleration safety limits specified in § 213.333. (5) *Measurement of wheel/rail forces.* For vehicle types intended to operate at track Class 7 speeds or above, or at any curving speed producing more than 6 inches of cant deficiency, qualification testing conducted over a representative segment of the route shall demonstrate that the vehicle type will not exceed the wheel/rail force safety limits specified in § 213.333. (2) *Carbody acceleration.* For vehicle types intended to operate at any curving speed producing more than 5 inches of cant deficiency, or at track Class 7 speeds and above, qualification testing conducted over a representative segment of the new route shall demonstrate that the vehicle type will not exceed the carbody lateral and vertical acceleration safety limits specified in § 213.333.
